text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- Demand for credits is low following high interest rates on loans asked by the banks.
- Hardships brought by economic reforms affect small private companies, the paper says.
- Private farmers will get credits with interest rates amounting to 55 percent.
- The Bucharest commodities exchange plans to call an international tender to sell old rolling stock and scrap iron.
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Some 49 percent of Romanians think their country is heading into the "right direction" while 69 percent fear high prices and the national currency's depreciation will affect their living standards, an opinion poll shows.
- The Bucharest-based Automatica SA is affected by an acute shortage of funds.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania is interested in developing good links with Germany, the paper quotes President Emil Constantinescu as saying.
- The state-run Avicola Codlea poultry farm cut 300 jobs.
- Licensed money exchange offices are confronted with a shortage of lei, the paper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Trade unions in the mining sector plan a two-hour warning strike on Thursday to protest against government plans to restructure the sector.
- The state-run Tarom SA airline will not cooperate with the local private DAC AIR airline, Tarom's general manager Dan Vulcan is quoted as saying.
- Romania has to cash $3.0 billion representing ex-communist era debts.
ADEVARUL
- The SNCFR railway authority will cut some 4,000 jobs.
- The restructuring process of Romania's industry proceeds at a slow pace, the paper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania will send special envoys to some NATO-member countries to lobby for its early admission into the alliance.
- Romania has better chances of quick NATO admission due to its new reformist government, German Economic Cooperation Minister Carl-Dieter Spranger said during a visit in Bucharest.
- The National Meteorological Institute warned of flood risks in the southern regions due to recent heavy rains.
ADEVARUL
- The government will issue ordinance to evacuate former communist officials who still live in state protocol houses, the newspaper says.
- Moldovan-made cigarettes are smuggled to Romania.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Razvan Temesan, ex-president of the state-owned Bancorex SA bank told a parliamentary commission Bancorex had given loans to some 100 top politicians of the ex-ruling Party of Social Democracy as well as to officials in the present ruling coalition.
- Dignitaries of the defunct Romanian Communist Party still live in luxury state-owned houses and pay meagre rents, said Valerian Stan, the head of the government's control body.
- The Court of Appeals will start on April hearings in the case of coalminers' leader Miron Cosma charged with undermining the state authority during the miners' riots in September 1991.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Only a radical institutional reform could place Romania on a list of priorities for NATO and the European Union admissions, former Polish finance minister Leszek Balcerowicz said during a visit to Bucharest. He praised Romania's government reform programme.

- Senate chairman Petre Roman met representatives of some 400,000 Jews born in Romania and now living in Israel and pledged to find solutions for the restitution of Jewish community properties confiscated by the communists.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
